rationale: Abstract studies adversarial rejection of safe requests by harmful-content safeguards and safety-aligned models, without an identified separate binary prompt-injection input-detector evaluation.
Abstract describes detecting and reversing attacks that bypass safety alignment to produce harmful responses; no separate binary input prompt-injection evaluation is identified.
Abstract uses injected instructions in service responses to disrupt or compromise an attacking LLM agent; it does not identify evaluation of a binary prompt-injection input classifier.
Abstract establishes layered prompt-injection input screening using rules, an ML classifier and a companion LLM before the target model. It does not establish the English-language evaluation setting.
